editorial:
Ever wonder how they made a giant green dragon look real before computers did everything? You get a front-row seat to all that chaos in this cool documentary. It takes you back to the set of Pete's Dragon, showing you the crazy puppets and the clever camera tricks the crew used to fool the audience. The vibe is super nostalgic and lighthearted, making you feel like you are hanging out with the actual artists who built the magic from scratch. It is less like a boring history lesson and more like a peek behind the curtain at a magic show.

What really hits home is seeing the trial and error involved in old-school effects. You will love seeing the mechanical parts of the dragon move and hearing the creators talk about their mistakes. The pacing is quick, though some of the older footage is a bit grainy. If you love movie trivia, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: The film wraps up by showing the final polished scenes from the movie side-by-side with the raw footage of the puppets. You see how the team blended the real actors with the animatronic dragon to make it look seamless. It concludes with a heartfelt look at how these old techniques paved the way for modern CGI, leaving you with a huge respect for the hard work that went into every single frame.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves movie magic and old Disney films.
